science.title: Effects of maximum teleportation distance on wayfinding in virtual reality: the role of optical flow cues
science.description: Instantaneous teleportation reduces simulator sickness risk by omitting continuous viewpoint motion but may impair spatial orientation. Previous research has generally examined maximum teleportation distance and optical-flow transitions separately, leaving their combined effects during wayfinding unclear. We conducted a 2 (teleportation type: no optical flow vs. brief optical flow) × 3 (maximum teleportation distance: 5, 15, and 25 m) mixed-design experiment with 60 participants who completed route-exploration and unguided-return tasks in a virtual urban environment. Wayfinding performance and experience were assessed using sketch maps, navigation measures, the Simulator Sickness Questionnaire, and semi-structured interviews. Sketch-map scores were lower at 25 m than at 5 and 15 m. Navigation time was longer at 5 m than at 25 m, and mean navigation time per teleportation increased across the 5-, 15-, and 25-m conditions. No significant between-type differences or type × distance interactions were detected for sketch-map or navigation measures. Simulator sickness scores were low across conditions. The aligned rank transform analysis indicated effects of teleportation type, distance, and their interaction that were not consistently reproduced by other approaches, leaving insufficient evidence for a stable simulator-sickness effect. Interview responses suggested that shorter-distance teleportation facilitated environmental observation, whereas longer-distance teleportation was perceived as easier to operate. The 25 m condition combined shorter navigation time with lower sketch-map scores. Distance conditions were paired with fixed scene variants, and the fixed 0.3 s transition coupled displacement with translation speed. The possible trade-off between traversal efficiency and environmental learning therefore remains specific to the tested configurations.

science.title: MambaSleepCVD for prediction of long term cardiovascular outcomes from polysomnography
science.description: Long-term cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk prediction remains a major global clinical priority. This study investigates how much prognostic information full-night polysomnography (PSG) carries after explicitly controlling demographic confounding, and whether combining specialized unimodal representations with continuous fusion mechanisms can effectively leverage it. We adopt a modular framework based on Coupled Mamba for simultaneous cross-modal and temporal fusion, capturing long-range dependencies and dynamic interactions between physiological modalities throughout sleep. With this capability, we assess whether specialized supervised representations from task-specific unimodal encoders offer prognostic value comparable to task-agnostic multimodal self-supervised pre-training. Validated on the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS) dataset, our approach achieves performance comparable to or better than current state-of-the-art architectures in the fully supervised, data-abundant regime, although the cardiac channel alone accounts for most of the discriminative signal. More importantly, we show that in the reference dataset chronological age strongly drives survival ranking; when provided as an explicit input, it can create a shortcut that obscures the contribution of PSG-derived physiology. Ultimately, our findings suggest that supervised unimodal experts integrated through a fusion engine provide a flexible pathway for prognostic risk ranking from sleep recordings, while reliable CVD screening will require independent external cohorts and explicit confounder control.

science.title: Expression patterns of Slc38a4 and mmu-miR-6948-3p in a murine model of metastatic triple-negative breast cancer
science.description: SLC38A4 (SNAT4), a system A amino acid transporter, contributes to nutrient uptake and metabolic regulation, but its role in the progression of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is unclear. We examined the expression of Slc38a4 and its predicted regulatory miRNA, mmu-miR-6948-3p, in primary tumors, invasive mammary tumors, and lung metastases in a murine TNBC model. RNA-sequencing data (GSE150928) from primary mammary tumors and lung metastases were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs), followed by functional enrichment, protein–protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, and miRNA–mRNA target prediction. Eighteen female BALB/c mice implanted with 4T1 TNBC cells were grouped into those with primary mammary tumors and those with lung metastases. Expression of Slc38a4 and mmu-miR-6948-3p was measured by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT–PCR). Public human datasets (TCGA, MET500, DepMap) were also examined. In the RNA-seq data, Slc38a4 was upregulated in lung metastases relative to primary tumors (logFC = 3.93) and was assigned to a PPI cluster enriched for amino acid transport and vesicle trafficking. qRT–PCR confirmed higher Slc38a4 expression in lung metastases (6.23 ± 0.48 vs. 1.00 ± 0.08, P < 0.0001) and lower expression in invasive mammary tumors (0.51 ± 0.05 vs. 1.00 ± 0.08, P < 0.0001) than in primary tumors. Levels of mmu-miR-6948-3p did not differ significantly between groups. In human data, SLC38A4 mRNA was lower in breast tumors than in normal breast tissue, and DNA methylation showed no clear relationship with its expression. Slc38a4 expression depends on tissue context during TNBC progression, being lower in invasive mammary tumors and higher in lung metastases, and this pattern is not explained by changes in mmu-miR-6948-3p. Functional studies are needed to determine whether the increase in the lung drives colonization or is an adaptive response to it.

science.title: Wrist photoplethysmography encodes dietary information
science.description: Whether wearable photoplethysmography (PPG) encodes dietary information remains unknown. We trained a language model on 1.1M meals to align PPG with meal descriptions. Near-meal PPG carries a meal-specific signal beyond individual traits; predictability decreases farther from meals. This transfers to dietary tasks: PPG increases AUC by 11% for a caloric-intake proxy and satiety across held-out and independent cohorts. Wearable PPG may augment text-based logging, compensating for brief descriptions.
